title: Release ORION — week slate, telemetry anchor, and variant brief (Apr 2026)
content:
Purpose
- Short working draft to align launch operators on the ORION feature-week rollout. Contains a compact calendar for the week, the oncall/operator preflight and launch checklists, telemetry smoke queries, variant-to-traffic mapping, abort criteria, and a first-pass release notes draft for product review.

Overview & objectives
- Goal: Ship ORION thin-client batching and prefix-KV cache improvements to hosted API and Dedicated pools with minimal customer impact.
- Success criteria (ops lens): no customer-facing errors >0.3% for 60m windows, median p50 latency regression <= +10ms, no spike in 5xx volume >2x baseline on any route.
- Known risky surfaces: model-variant fallback, KV cache eviction under heavy multi-tenant workloads, and older SDKs that might send large system prompts.

Week calendar (high level) — Apr 12–18, 2026
- Mon Apr 12: Dry-run in staging; smoke job runs at 09:00 UTC and 16:00 UTC. Telemetry anchor validation.
- Tue Apr 13: Canary rollout to 1% traffic for hosted-api routes only; monitoring window 3h. Ops standby 08:00–20:00 PT.
- Wed Apr 14: Expand canary to 5% if metrics green; begin Dedicated pool pilot (shadow traffic) for two customers.
- Thu Apr 15: A/B experiment for batching knob (intensive token workloads); observe cost delta.
- Fri Apr 16: Decision day — ramp to 20% or roll back. Finalize customer-facing release notes.
- Sat/Sun Apr 17–18: Quiet weekend with oncall watchlist; no further ramps.

Preflight checklist (48–24h before first canary)
- [ ] Confirm all PRs merged to release branch; list attached in linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Integration tests green (end-to-end + perf harness) at head.
- [ ] Staging smoke run: run smoke.sh (s3://redwood-staging/logs/orion-smoke-2026-04-12) and validate against smoke baseline.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards created and pinned: latency, 5xx, error traces, model-fallback-rate, CPU/GPU throttle.
- [ ] Slack channel #release-orion created and escalations template posted.
- [ ] Paging rotation defined: primary/secondary/backfill names in oncall rota doc.
- [ ] Rollout config uploaded to release-config service with canary percent/rollout cadence.

Launch hour checklist (when moving canary percentage)
- Operator 1 (initiator): trigger rollout with release service, annotate change in #release-orion and in JIRA-RELEASE-7890.
- Operator 2 (observer): open latency and error dashboards, run quick KV cache sanity query (see telemetry below).
- Operator 3 (safety): ready with rollback plan and pre-auth to run rollback playbook if abort criteria met.
- Post-deploy smoke (0–5m): generator: 1000 synthetic requests across 10 routes; check failure rate.
- 5–15m: tail logs for new stack traces; run trace sampler against top 3 services.
- 15–60m: verify business KPIs (token throughput, burst throttles, billing spikes).

Operator post-launch tasks (if green)
- [ ] Capture canary snapshot (automated) and tag release-config with timestamp.
- [ ] Note anomalies in the rollout journal (link to S3).
- [ ] Begin slow ramp according to week calendar.

Telemetry smoke queries & tips (quick copy-paste)
- Active error-rate check (time series): sum(rate(errors_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (route) -> flag routes >0.003
- Latency distribution: histogram_quantile(0.5, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) and 0.95 for regression checks.
- Model fallback rate: increase in model_fallbacks_total / requests_total -> flag >0.01
- KV cache miss skew: topk(10, sum(kv_cache_misses_total{pool!~"test.*"}) by (customer)) -> look for sudden concentrated misses.
- GPU util + queue depth: avg by gpu_id of (gpu_utilization_percent) and queue_length gauge -> if queue_length spikes while utilization low, suspect scheduling bug.

Variant mapping and customer scope
- Variant A (orion-v1): default behavior, enabled in hosted-api for all routes in canary phase.
- Variant B (orion-v1-quant): quantized kernel path, only for Dedicated shadow customers.
- Variant C (orion-v1-safe): conservative cache eviction, forced for customers with strict P99 SLOs during pilot (two named pilot customers).
- Traffic map for Tue canary: hosted-api routes = 1% to Variant A; all other traffic = baseline.

Abort criteria (immediate rollback triggers)
- Any single route 5xx rate >2% sustained for 10m.
- Overall customer error-rate >0.5% for 30m.
- P50 latency regression exceeding +30ms for 15m or p95 > +200ms for 15m.
- New OOMs in inference services or GPU driver/kernel crashes.
- Two or more distinct customers report production failures via SC/CS portal within the monitoring window.

Rollback procedure (fast)
- Operator triggers release-service rollback to previous release-config (button or CLI).
- Post-rollback: clear canary annotation, notify #release-orion, open emergency incident channel, and capture debug traces.
- Follow-up: run forensics checklist and schedule 2h postmortem if rollback was due to platform regression.

Communications (internal & external)
- Internal: Use #release-orion for all notes; use the pinned message for runbook. Escalate to ENG VP if rollback occurs.
- Customer-facing: Draft below but do not publish until product sign-off. Notify pilot customers (email templates in Confluence-1234).

Draft release notes (first-pass — product to edit)
- Headline: Faster inference for multi-prompt workloads (ORION rollout)
- Short summary: ORION introduces adaptive batching and prefix-KV caching improvements that reduce median inference latency for multi-prompt applications and lowers per-token CPU utilization.
- Impact: Customers using streaming and batch routes should see lower costs and slightly reduced tail latency. A small percentage of very long system-prompts may see different cache behavior; customers on Dedicated can opt into the quantized kernel path for extra savings.
- Rollout: Gradual over the week; no expected downtime.
- Notes for SDK users: Older SDK versions (< v1.3.4) may need a minor patch to avoid sending large system prompts which can interact poorly with prefix caching.

Open questions / TODOs
- Who owns the customer email for pilot-customer-2? (Rina to confirm)
- Add a quick harness job that simulates 10k concurrent short-chat sessions (ticket in linked_artifacts).
- Verify cost-monitoring dashboard for Dedicated pilot (Liam).

Annex: quick links and artifacts
- Release config & annotations: github.com/redwood/release-configs/orion/1.0
- Perf harness: github.com/redwood/perf/harness/orion-smoke
- Forensics template: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Ticket (launch): JIRA-RELEASE-7890

Notes to reviewers
- This is a compact operational-week slate — please review abort criteria and telemetry queries first. If you have a different tolerance for p50 vs p95, call it out here.
- If we green-light Tue canary, Ops will hold the ramp schedule and only proceed on unanimous green from primary observer and safety.

-- Aisha (release owner)
- quick notes to self: watch the KV miss concentration pattern after 30m; if it shows customer concentration, move to Variant C gating for that customer.
